submission.justification: Provisional recommendation only. Algorithm-L2 at 36 GeV has the highest simulated signal efficiency in the scan (93.004%, vs 92.742% at the 35 GeV grid point, 84.414% best for L3, 74.248% best for L1). However, the latency requirement, which the brief defines as a hard limit of 4.0 us, has not been verified for any candidate: latency_values_found = 0, latency_check_passed_count = 0, latency_verified_candidates = 0, and latency_compliance_confirmed = 0. The latency budget document was not found. So I cannot confirm that L2 meets the hard latency constraint, and L2 must not be deployed until its FPGA latency is measured and shown to be at or below 4.0 us. The allocated-rate check is also weak: the results give efficiency at 8 kHz but no recorded rate values for any threshold, so the 8 kHz rate compliance of the 36 GeV working point is unverified. The gain over the 35 GeV grid point (0.26 percentage points) is small. Neighbouring fine-scan points are not monotonic (34 GeV 92.379%, 36 GeV 93.004%, 37 GeV 92.267%), which suggests the 36 GeV value may be within statistical fluctuation. A threshold near 35 to 36 GeV is a reasonable working point once latency and rate are confirmed.

Recommended threshold is 36 GeV, inside the 20 to 60 GeV range.
